body:
**Needs security sign-off — Travis gives the final look; do not merge before.** Travis approved this in principle on 2026-10-13 (finish after the third Aggressive milestone run, then final review before merge). Refs #505.

## What changes
- **Approval for every command at confirmation.** When a person confirms Aggressive in `/security`, every Corbanu pane and child agent of this Corbanu Terminal on that home requires a person's approval for every command that isn't known read-only (`untrusted`, reviewer: you), from its next turn. Panes started later in this process, before the restart, start that way.
- **Stored settings, not a per-turn override** (review r1 blocker 2). Each thread's stored settings change at confirmation, through the same update `/approvals` uses. So steering, injected items, child-agent messages, MCP tool approvals and `/status` all see the same value.
  - A turn that is already running when you confirm keeps its old policy until it ends, as after any approval change.
  - Until the restart a later settings update can't lower it. The TUI replays its approval policy with every turn.
- **A managed requirement is never overridden** (review r1 blocker 1). If a managed approval-policy or reviewer requirement rules out `untrusted` or a person as reviewer, nothing changes in that thread. The thread gets a warning, and screen 07 lists it under "not applied".
- **Still restart-only:** the sandbox, network and web search, environment stripping, the credential broker and the child-agent rules. The texts say so, and screen 07 reports what the confirmation actually did:
  - how many threads hold it;
  - which kept their settings, and why;
  - which were still applying.
  The restart list keeps the approval row whenever no thread holds it.
- **Not covered:** `corbanu exec`, IDE sessions and other processes, as today; they get it when they start under Aggressive. Internal sessions (reviews, compaction, memory, the automatic reviewer's own sessions) also keep their settings.
- **Permissive is unchanged** unless someone confirms Aggressive. Lowering to Permissive keeps the approvals until the restart, like Core's other protections, and the review says so.
- **Before the restart:** a session that had `never` or granular approvals now asks a person where requests used to be rejected automatically. Its own sandbox still applies until the restart.

## Design
- `core/src/security/confirmed_approvals.rs` holds the confirmed homes and this process's sessions. Homes are canonicalised (#619). `commit_human_level_change` calls `confirm` only for a live commit whose target and committed level are both Aggressive.
- `core/src/session/confirmed_aggressive.rs` applies it through `update_settings` and then emits `ThreadSettingsApplied`. It reports "held" only after reading the stored settings back.
- `SessionConfiguration` gains `aggressive_approvals`. `apply()` ignores approval and reviewer updates while it is set, and returns the requirement's error when setting it is ruled out.

## Gate (head 8c9168a1a8; codex-rs identical to 5680e2b420)
- **Fail-before/pass-after regression tests:** `core/tests/suite/issue_505.rs`, plus unit tests in `session/confirmed_aggressive_tests.rs` and `security/confirmed_approvals_tests.rs`, plus picker tests.
  - **Against the round-1 head 15c6627e97:**
    - the stored-settings approval test fails;
    - steering during a later turn fails (`AuthorizationChanged`);
    - a child-agent message during a later turn is never delivered (30 s timeout);
    - running children and later threads fail;
    - with a managed reviewer, the turn ran `untrusted` with reviewer User instead of the managed `on-request` with AutoReview.
  - **Against main 45bfa7d938:** the approval test and the children/later-threads test fail.
  - **This head:** all pass.
- **Focused `just test`** (`-p codex-core -p codex-tui`; filters security, issue_, pf_2, request_permissions, protected, grant, session::, pending_input, approval, thread_settings, authorization, steer, permission; TMPDIR=/tmp): 1682 of 1682 pass without developer-accounting and 1682 of 1682 with it.
- **Clippy `-D warnings`:**
  - macOS (core, tui): clean, plain and with developer-accounting.
  - Linux (glitch, `ulimit -n 65536`, 5680e2b420): clean, plain and with developer-accounting.
  - Windows: `rust-ci-full` run 38507299010 on 5680e2b420, clean. An earlier run flagged unused imports in a unix-only test; that is fixed.
- **Independent review (Opus 5.5 High):**
  - r2: APPROVE, with 2 should-fixes and nits; fixed in 5680e2b420.
  - r3: APPROVE on 5680e2b420.
  - r4: APPROVE on the exact head 8c9168a1a8. The change since r3 is the blob allowlist and demo files only.
- **tmux check** (disposable home, GLM 5.3 Flash on zai), starting from approvals `never` and workspace-write:
  - after confirming, the agent's `printf ok > issue505.txt` waits for approval; declined, so no file;
  - in `/new`, `/status` shows "Next turn: Custom (workspace, untrusted)" and the same command asks.
- **SOP video:** [issue-505 approvals at confirmation](https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/releases/download/demos/issue-505-issue505-approvals-at-confirmation-5549054ff93f-2026-10-13.mp4) (35 s).
- **CI note:** `core/src/session/tests.rs` is already over the 512000-byte blob limit on main (512109 bytes, since #687). This PR adds one fixture field, so the file is allowlisted in `.github/blob-size-allowlist.txt`. It should be split later.

## Open review nits (not done; follow-ups if wanted)
- Screen 07 keys the restart list on `held > 0`. When everything is still pending it understates; it never overstates.
- "Every command" doesn't mention two cases:
  - app tools with `apps.<id>.approvals_reviewer = auto_review` still go to the automatic reviewer;
  - `/review` runs its commands with `never`.
  Both are the same after the restart.
- If the TUI rolls back its level file after Core has committed (rare), threads stay held and the failure message doesn't say so. This is stricter than claimed, not looser.
- Optional tests not written: a confirmation racing a session start, resume or fork after confirmation, and an integration test for a managed approval-policy pin (it is unit-tested).
